To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SMOS and AMSRE products are complementary, that the AMSRE data are more accurate over regions with sparse LAI and that both products have comparable performance over regions with dense LAI.

the AMSR E and the SMOS SSM products have a high degree of consistency with the SSM estimates produced by the ECMWF LDAS, and that the SMOS SMM product is more suitable than the AMSR E product for monitoring the temporal variability of soil moisture in highly vegetated regions.

the AMSR E and SMOS soil moisture products have a similar performance in terms of correlation with the ECMWF LDAS soil moisture estimates, with a slight edge for SMOS over arid and sparsely vegetated areas, and for AMSR E over semi arid areas.

the development of a methodology for evaluating satellite derived SSM products and their potential for assimilation into the LDAS.

the evaluation of the quality and the accuracy of two new SSM products, SMOSL and AMSRM, with respect to a reference SSM product (SM DAS 2) over a wide range of vegetation densities, and it is the first study of this kind.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SMOS and/or AMSR E SSM products can be considered as reliable data sources for SSM monitoring at global scale, and that the SMOS and AMSRE data records can be combined in a systematic way in order to monitor SSM variability at global scale, in particular over regions where vegetation density is high.
SMOS and SMAP will provide the most accurate SSM products in regions where LAI is low to moderately low, whereas AMSR E will provide the most valuable data records over regions with high LAI.
SMOSL3 is the best performing product for most of the vegetated biomes, whereas AMSRM is the best performing for most of the arid and semi-arid biomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SMOS and the AMSR E are complementary and that both are useful in monitoring the SSM.
SMOS and SMAP (Soil Moistur e Active Passive) are complementary.
both SMOS and SMAP will provide a valuable source of SSM data, but the two missions will be complementary in their ability to monitor land-atmosphere processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SMOS and AMSRE SSM data products have a high potential to improve the quality of SSM data assimilation and to advance the science of land surface hydrology.
SMOS and/or AMSR E can be used to monitor SSM over a large fraction of the globe, with the exception of the densest forests.
